$comment: The Incident RCA history tables (ADR 0031), version 1: what NB_DatabaseHub_LiveActivity writes to LH_DatabaseHub, what SM_DatabaseHub_History reads, and what the Insights app queries. The notebook, the semantic model, and the app test against this file; rca/README.md explains it. Types are the notebook's TABLE_COLUMNS types; model types are TMDL data types.

string.document: index into the document's strings, or null

timestamp.document: integer milliseconds after the document's epochUtc, or null

date.document: not in the document: the notebook derives it

notebookColumns.name: run_id
notebookColumns.description: The notebook's RUN_ID: session-<SESSION_ID> for a control session, as the other history tables.

notebookColumns.name: document_id
notebookColumns.description: The evidence document the row came from (documentId).

notebookColumns.name: report_date_utc
notebookColumns.description: The UTC date of the row's primary time; relates the table to Date, as the other history tables.

tables.name: rca_sessions
tables.grain: One session in one sample of a blocking chain: every session that waits on another, and every session another waits on.

columns.name: captured_at_utc
columns.description: When the observer took the sample (UTC).

columns.name: target
columns.description: T1, T2, T3, T4, or T4-replica.

columns.name: session_id
columns.description: The SQL Server session_id (SPID) or the PostgreSQL pid.

columns.name: blocked_by
columns.description: Comma-separated IDs of the sessions this one waits on (SQL Server: blocking_session_id, including the documented negative owners; PostgreSQL: pg_blocking_pids, or the lock's holders from pg_locks). Null when it isn't blocked.

columns.name: status
columns.description: SQL Server: the request's status when the session has a request (running, runnable, suspended), else the session's (sleeping). PostgreSQL: pg_stat_activity.state (active, idle, idle in transaction).

columns.name: wait_type
columns.description: SQL Server wait_type, or PostgreSQL wait_event_type:wait_event.

columns.name: wait_ms
columns.description: How long the current wait has lasted.

columns.name: wait_resource
columns.description: SQL Server wait_resource; PostgreSQL's lock tag (locktype and its fields).

columns.name: lock_resource_type
columns.description: KEY, PAGE, RID, OBJECT, XACT (SQL Server); relation, tuple, transactionid (PostgreSQL).

columns.name: lock_object
columns.description: The locked table, [schema].[table] on SQL Server or schema.table on PostgreSQL, when the lock names one.

columns.name: lock_index
columns.description: The locked index, for KEY and PAGE locks.

columns.name: lock_mode_wanted
columns.description: The mode this session waits for.

columns.name: lock_mode_held
columns.description: The mode this session holds on the resource others wait for.

columns.name: open_transactions
columns.description: Open transactions (SQL Server open_transaction_count; PostgreSQL 1 when xact_start is set).

columns.name: transaction_age_ms
columns.description: How long its oldest open transaction has been open.

columns.name: idle_ms
columns.description: How long an idle session (sleeping, or idle in transaction) has been idle.

columns.name: login_name
columns.description: The login or role. The workload's own sessions only; null for any other session.

columns.name: host_name
columns.description: The client host. The workload's own sessions only.

columns.name: program_name
columns.description: The application name as a DBA would see it, without the workload's internal segments (rca/README.md, Names). The workload's own sessions only.

columns.name: run_token
columns.description: An opaque token shared by the sessions of one workload run, so the rules can group them; it names nothing (rca/README.md, Names).

columns.name: module_name
columns.description: The stored procedure or function the statement belongs to: [schema].[name] on SQL Server, the called function on PostgreSQL.

columns.name: statement_text
columns.description: The running statement, or the last one for an idle session, normalized (literals replaced, at most 2,000 characters).

columns.name: input_buffer
columns.description: SQL Server's input buffer for an idle session (the last batch or RPC), normalized.

columns.name: backend_type
columns.description: PostgreSQL backend_type (client backend, startup, walreceiver, walsender).

columns.name: is_demo
columns.description: True for the demo workload's own sessions, the baseline's and any fault's alike, which keep text, login, and host; false for any other session, which arrives without them.

tables.name: rca_waits
tables.grain: One wait type's delta over one phase of a capture episode: the episode itself, or the baseline just before it.

columns.name: target
columns.description: T1, T2, or T3.

columns.name: episode_id
columns.description: The observer's capture episode (rca_events kind capture, event_name escalated, code) the row belongs to.

columns.name: phase
columns.description: baseline (the minutes before the episode) or episode.

columns.name: window_start_utc
columns.description: Start of the delta's window.

columns.name: window_end_utc
columns.description: End of the delta's window.

columns.name: wait_type
columns.description: The wait type.

columns.name: wait_category
columns.description: Its category from Learn's wait categories mapping table.

columns.name: wait_ms
columns.description: Wait time in the window.

columns.name: waiting_tasks
columns.description: Waits that ended in the window.

columns.name: signal_ms
columns.description: Signal wait time in the window.

columns.name: max_wait_ms
columns.description: The longest single wait seen (the cumulative maximum when it rose in the window).

tables.name: rca_events
tables.grain: One server-side event, or one count of identical events per minute: an error, an attention, a deadlock, a lock escalation, a tuning change, or the observer's own capture escalation.

columns.name: event_time_utc
columns.description: When it happened; for a count, the start of its minute.

columns.name: target
columns.description: T1 to T5, or T4-replica.

columns.name: kind
columns.description: error, attention, deadlock, escalation, tuning, or capture.

columns.name: event_name
columns.description: The source event: the Extended Events event (error_reported, attention, xml_deadlock_report, database_xml_deadlock_report, lock_escalation), the counter (pg_stat_database.deadlocks), the tuning change, or for capture: escalated or relaxed.

columns.name: session_id
columns.description: The session the event belongs to; for a deadlock, its victim.

columns.name: program_name
columns.description: As in RCA Sessions: the workload's own sessions only, without internal segments.

columns.name: run_token
columns.description: As in RCA Sessions.

columns.name: login_name
columns.description: The workload's own sessions only.

columns.name: host_name
columns.description: The workload's own sessions only.

columns.name: module_name
columns.description: The module the event's statement belongs to.

columns.name: code
columns.description: The SQL Server error number or the PostgreSQL SQLSTATE; for capture, the episode's ID.

columns.name: severity
columns.description: The SQL Server error severity.

columns.name: intercepted
columns.description: True when the statement's own TRY...CATCH handled the error (error_reported's is_intercepted).

columns.name: event_count
columns.description: 1 for one event; the count when identical events are counted per minute.

columns.name: object_name
columns.description: The object the event names: the escalated table, a deadlock's first resource, the tuned query.

columns.name: lock_mode
columns.description: The lock mode of an escalation.

columns.name: detail
columns.description: The event in plain words, normalized: the error message, the escalation's lock counts, the tuning state, or the signal and value that started or ended a capture episode.

columns.name: deadlock_json
columns.description: For a deadlock: its graph reduced to JSON (rca/README.md, Deadlocks).

tables.name: rca_queries
tables.grain: One Query Store plan over one phase of a capture episode.

columns.name: target
columns.description: T1, T2, or T3.

columns.name: episode_id
columns.description: The observer's capture episode.

columns.name: phase
columns.description: baseline or episode.

columns.name: interval_start_utc
columns.description: Start of the Query Store intervals summed.

columns.name: interval_end_utc
columns.description: End of the Query Store intervals summed.

columns.name: query_id
columns.description: Query Store query_id.

columns.name: plan_id
columns.description: Query Store plan_id.

columns.name: query_hash
columns.description: The query hash, as hex.

columns.name: module_name
columns.description: The module the query belongs to.

columns.name: statement_text
columns.description: The query text, normalized.

columns.name: executions
columns.description: Executions in the phase.

columns.name: cpu_ms
columns.description: Total CPU time.

columns.name: duration_ms
columns.description: Total duration.

columns.name: logical_reads
columns.description: Total logical reads.

columns.name: physical_reads
columns.description: Total physical reads.

columns.name: log_bytes
columns.description: Total log bytes used.

columns.name: max_used_memory_kb
columns.description: The largest memory grant used.

columns.name: max_dop
columns.description: The highest degree of parallelism.

columns.name: plans_for_query
columns.description: How many plans the query had in Query Store.

columns.name: is_forced_plan
columns.description: True when the plan is forced.

columns.name: plan_forcing_type
columns.description: MANUAL or AUTO when forced.

tables.name: rca_resource
tables.grain: One counter or resource sample, in long format: the sentinel's counters, and the resource samples of capture episodes.

columns.name: at_utc
columns.description: When the sample was taken; for a delta, the end of its interval.

columns.name: target
columns.description: T1 to T5, or T4-replica.

columns.name: source
columns.description: The capture ID that read it (rca/capture/README.md).

columns.name: metric
columns.description: The metric's name (rca/README.md, Resource metrics).

columns.name: value
columns.description: The value: a gauge's reading, or a counter's delta over the interval.

columns.name: unit
columns.description: count, percent, ms, bytes, or per second.

tables.name: rca_replica
tables.grain: One replay sample from one side of T4's replication: the read replica's replay state and conflicts, or the primary's view of the standby.

columns.name: at_utc
columns.description: When the sample was taken.

columns.name: target
columns.description: T4-replica for the replica's side, T4 for the primary's.

columns.name: side
columns.description: replica or primary.

columns.name: standby_name
columns.description: The primary's name for the standby (pg_stat_replication.application_name).

columns.name: since_last_replayed_s
columns.description: now() minus pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp() on the replica.

columns.name: received_not_replayed_bytes
columns.description: pg_last_wal_receive_lsn() minus pg_last_wal_replay_lsn() on the replica.

columns.name: replay_lag_s
columns.description: pg_stat_replication.replay_lag on the primary.

columns.name: write_lag_s
columns.description: pg_stat_replication.write_lag on the primary.

columns.name: flush_lag_s
columns.description: pg_stat_replication.flush_lag on the primary.

columns.name: send_gap_bytes
columns.description: The primary's current WAL position minus what it sent.

columns.name: wal_bytes_per_s
columns.description: WAL the primary generated per second since the previous sample (pg_stat_wal).

columns.name: startup_wait
columns.description: The replica's startup (replay) process wait, wait_event_type:wait_event.

columns.name: conflict_relation
columns.description: The table whose lock replay waits for, from pg_locks.

columns.name: conflict_wanted_mode
columns.description: The lock mode replay waits for (AccessExclusiveLock).

columns.name: conflict_wait_start_utc
columns.description: When replay started to wait (pg_locks.waitstart).

columns.name: conflict_holder_session
columns.description: The replica query's pid that holds the conflicting lock.

columns.name: conflict_holder_mode
columns.description: The holder's lock mode.

columns.name: conflict_holder_program
columns.description: The holder's application name, as program_name in RCA Sessions.

columns.name: conflict_holder_run_token
columns.description: As run_token in RCA Sessions.

columns.name: conflict_holder_statement
columns.description: The holder's statement, normalized.

columns.name: conflicts_cancelled
columns.description: Queries the replica cancelled for conflicts since the previous sample (pg_stat_database_conflicts).

columns.name: max_standby_streaming_delay_s
columns.description: The replica's max_standby_streaming_delay.

tables.name: rca_coverage
tables.grain: What the observer captured for one target over one document's window, and what it didn't, with why.

columns.name: target
columns.description: T1 to T5, or T4-replica.

columns.name: window_start_utc
columns.description: Start of the window.

columns.name: window_end_utc
columns.description: End of the window.

columns.name: captured
columns.description: True when the sentinel ran for the whole window.

columns.name: sources
columns.description: Comma-separated capture IDs that returned rows.

columns.name: gaps
columns.description: One gap per line: what wasn't captured and why (a permission, a timeout, the export's budget).

tables.name: rca_answer_key
tables.grain: One fault the workload injected (kind run) or one event it reported about its own fault (kind run-event): the answer key, which only the scoreboard and the tests read.

columns.name: kind
columns.description: run (one injected fault, start to end) or run-event (an event the workload reported about it).

columns.name: target
columns.description: T1 to T5, or T4-replica.

columns.name: event_time_utc
columns.description: The run's start, or the event's time.

columns.name: end_time_utc
columns.description: The run's end.

columns.name: scenario
columns.description: The scenario ID (scenarios/<id>).

columns.name: scenario_run_id
columns.description: The runner's run ID.

columns.name: run_token
columns.description: The run's opaque token, which the detection tables carry, so grading can check that a blind finding names the injected run's sessions.

columns.name: event_name
columns.description: For run-event: the event's name (demo.scenario_run_events).

columns.name: outcome
columns.description: For run: Completed, Stopped, TimedOut, or Failed.

columns.name: detail
columns.description: The run's parameters, or the event's detail.

relationshipNotes: Every table relates to Target and Date, as the other history tables. None relates to Incident Windows or Scenario Runs: the detection tables never meet the answer key in the model, and a second path from Target would make the model ambiguous.

measures.name: Blocked Sessions (captured)
measures.description: The most sessions blocked in one sample in context.
measures.definition: MAXX ( VALUES ( 'RCA Sessions'[Captured At UTC] ), CALCULATE ( COUNTROWS ( 'RCA Sessions' ), NOT ISBLANK ( 'RCA Sessions'[Blocked By] ) ) )

measures.name: Head Blocker Idle (s)
measures.description: The longest a head blocker (a session others wait on that waits on no one) sat idle, in seconds.
measures.definition: The maximum Idle (ms) / 1000 over sessions whose Session ID appears in another row's Blocked By in the same sample and whose own Blocked By is blank.

measures.name: Errors (captured)
measures.description: Errors the observer captured, intercepted ones included.

measures.name: Replica Replay Stall (s)
measures.description: The longest the read replica went without replaying a transaction, in seconds.
measures.definition: CALCULATE ( MAX ( 'RCA Replica'[Since Last Replayed (s)] ), 'RCA Replica'[Side] = "replica" )

measures.name: Injected Faults
measures.description: Faults the workload injected (the scoreboard and the tests only).
measures.definition: CALCULATE ( COUNTROWS ( 'RCA Answer Key' ), 'RCA Answer Key'[Kind] = "run" )
